wtv-scramble — render pipeline benchmark

Standalone A/B benchmark of the Block Permute render path: the shipped v1.2.0 pipeline (Pipeline A, many <video> reads per frame) vs. the fixed pipeline (Pipeline B, exactly one <video> read per frame). Runs entirely in this tab — no server, no network, nothing to install.

What this proves

Firefox re-pays the video→canvas colorspace/decode conversion on every drawImage(video, …) call, while Chrome converts the decoded frame once and reuses it for the rest of that task. The shipped renderer draws straight from the <video> element 1 (base layer) + grid² (tiles) times per frame — 82 reads at grid 9 — so its cost scales with grid² against the most expensive possible source. The fix snapshots the video into an offscreen canvas once per frame, then sources every tile from that canvas instead.

  • Pipeline A (old, v1.2.0 structure): 1× drawImage(video) full-frame base layer into an intermediate canvas, + grid²× drawImage(video, tile…) into that same canvas, + 1× final blit of that canvas onto the visible canvas.
  • Pipeline B (new, fixed): 1× drawImage(video) into a reused offscreen snapshot canvas, + up to 2× border-strip copies from the snapshot, + grid²× tile copies from the snapshot straight onto the visible canvas. Zero further video-element reads that frame.

Both pipelines use the identical permutation, identical tile rects, and the identical synthetic source frame stream — the only variable under test is whether tiles are sourced from the <video> element or from a pre-snapshotted <canvas>.

Run it

Synthesizes its own animated video locally (canvas → captureStream(30)) — nothing is downloaded and nothing leaves this tab. Tests grid 9 then grid 3, each pipeline timed for 5 seconds, first 10 frames of every window discarded as warmup. Takes about 20 seconds total.

Pipeline A — old (video-sourced tiles)
Intermediate work canvas, full-frame base + tiles, then blitted to this visible canvas.
Pipeline B — new (canvas-sourced tiles)
One video snapshot per frame; border strips + tiles drawn straight onto this visible canvas.
